rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.2-2.3 - own field spectro-radiometer measurements of 213 diseased and 201 healthy grapevine leaf samples (four varieties, PACA region, two campaigns in 2016), disease status confirmed by inspector and PCR. Q2: Section 3.3-3.4, Tables 6-11 and Discussion - SDIs built from GA-selected wavelengths reached 100% accuracy for individual varieties in August and September versus 90-98% for the best common SVIs (Tables 6, 7 vs 9, 10); authors conclude SDIs gave in general higher accuracy than SVIs, measurements acquired under production conditions directly in the field (Section 1, 2.2). Q8: Discussion last paragraph - no single best index for FD in all situations; SDIs depend on infestation level and variety; indices need testing on other varieties, changing environments, scales and field conditions; only tested when foliar symptoms visible; discrimination from Bois Noir not tested; Conclusions - leaf scale only, two other FD symptoms not detectable spectrally.
rows.notes: Study directly supports the passage as worded (SDI vs common SVIs detection accuracy in field-acquired data); it shows detection/differentiation only, not disease control - the pest_control function is inferred by the extractor from the following sentence. Q3: single method (SVM classification of leaf spectra); PCR/inspector only provide ground truth. Q4: reflectance differences shown (Fig. 9) but no pigment or physiological intermediate measured. Q5: four cultivars of one crop in one region. Q6: leaf-level only. Q7: authors note index must be tailored per variety and severity, treated here as a dependency rather than a stated requirement; scale corrections are recommendations. Q9: accuracies are 10-fold CV means with no SD/CI; AUC and FNR/FPR are not dispersion. Note: ARI outperformed SDIs in some combined-data cases (red varieties, all data, September/combined campaigns) and complete spectra were better for some combined cases.

rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.2-2.3 - own field spectral measurements of healthy and FD-infected grapevine leaves of four varieties, two campaigns in 2016.
rows.notes: The study reports only leaf-level classification accuracy of SDIs versus common SVIs for FD detection; it measures no yield, fruit quality, management action or production outcome. Yield losses from FD are mentioned only in the Introduction from cited sources. Detection accuracy is at most a precondition for the crop_production effect (avoiding yield/quality losses) attributed by the extractor.

notes: Full text available including appendix tables; some pages have garbled duplicated text from PDF extraction but content is readable. Study is a primary field spectroscopy study at leaf scale in one French region (PACA), four grapevine cultivars, one season.
